A row is `duplicate_in_file` when an earlier row has the same email … it is `email_exists` when a user with that email already exists. The later of two clashing rows is the one flagged. Existing users are never changed.
an imported user is indistinguishable from one made through single-create in role … a header named `password` or `role` is rejected as an unknown column
verdicts.missing: File-supplied roles are rejected outright. The spec does not establish that the default role assigned by single-create is within the importing admin’s own authority.

and a header row. Header names are trimmed and case-insensitive; exactly `email` and `name`, each once, in any order, and no other column. … `invalid_header` (with `missing`, `unknown`, `duplicate` lists)
The file must be UTF-8 (an optional leading BOM is ignored), comma-delimited, with LF or CRLF line ends, quoted fields per RFC 4180 (commas, doubled quotes and line breaks inside quotes)
effects that leave the system (onboarding email or similar, per G-4) happen only after the whole import has been durably committed, and never for users of a rejected import.
at `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` accepted, one byte over refused; at `IMPORT_MAX_ROWS` accepted, one row over refused.

submit FX-1 (201), then submit FX-1 again → 422 `row_errors` with three `email_exists` entries (rows 1–3, lines 2–4); the store holds exactly 3 users, not 6.
process in the request. … if the NFR-1 probe shows a file at the chosen limit does not finish inside the platform request ceiling, move to an asynchronous design

verdicts.missing: The recovery flow calls for a corrected upload. It does not specify an explicit cancellation action during processing or a way to retry just the flagged rows from the original attempt.

verdicts.missing: The busy indicator is specified, but the maximum-file completion deadline is only relative to an unmeasured platform timeout. No concrete duration is set.
